To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integrated design of sustainable buildings is a conjecture/analysis (C/A) process where the architects and engineers share the character of designer and work together in a team, with the client.
the design process in the sustainable building design is closer to the conjecture/analysis model.

the integrated design process is closer to a conjecture/analysis (C/A) process than to the analysis/synthesis (A/S) process; that the architect and the engineer are both designers and that the architect and engineer share the character of designer; and that in the integrated design process the architect and the engineering team work as equals, sharing the same level of responsibility and the same role of designers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of integrated design process for sustainable design, based on an analysis of the current practice of integrated design in the construction industry.
the design process in the field of sustainable design.
understanding the design process of sustainable design in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the integrated design of sustainable buildings can be described as a Conjecture / Analysis (C/A) process that involves a series of conjectures and analyses, in which the architects and engineers work in parallel, sharing the character and responsibilities of designers.
the integrated design approach in the practice of sustainability is closer to a conjecture/analysis process.

the Integrated Design Process in the practice of Sustainable Design is a C/A process that is characterized by the following elements; a) a shared responsibility among architects and engineers in the design process, b) the use of the design process to achieve a sustainable building, c) a holistic approach to the problem, d) a holistic approach in the solution and, e) an iterative process that allows for the continuous improvement of the building design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of a sustainable building is a process of conjecture/analysis that is integrated and collaborative, where both the architect and engineer are designers.

sustainable design requires a new understanding of the integrated design process, which is not a linear sequence of steps, but a continuous process of conjecture, analysis, evaluation and re-conjecture.
the Integrated Design Process in sustainable design is a Conjecture Analysis (C/A) process, in which the designer proposes an idea before attempting to do analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Integrated Design Process is closer to a C/A model, where architects and engineers proceed as conjecture-makers, sharing the character and responsibility of designer, and where both architects and engineers are involved in analysis and synthesis.
the integrated design approach is not limited to the traditional A/S process, but can be found in a C/A process.
the Integrated Design Process is not a linear process, but a cyclical one, with the architect and engineer acting as designers, and with conjectures and analyses being made simultaneously.
